chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washsha', from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abdullah ibn Sulayman, who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) speaking, while in his presence was a man from the people of al-Basra called Uthman the Blind, who was saying: 'Al-Hasan al-Basri alleges that those who conceal knowledge will harm the inhabitants of the Fire by the odor of their bellies.'

So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Then the Believer of the people of Pharaoh has perished! Knowledge has not ceased to be concealed since God sent Noah (peace be upon him). So let al-Hasan go right and left — by God, knowledge will not be found except here.'

key_terms.الْعِلْمُ: knowledge; sacred religious knowledge exclusively held and transmitted by the Ahl al-Bayt
key_terms.مُؤْمِنُ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ: the Believer of the people of Pharaoh (Quran 40:28), who hid his faith to protect Moses (AS)
key_terms.هَاهُنَا: here — the Imam's deictic gesture toward himself as the exclusive locus of true knowledge
key_terms.يَكْتُمُونَ: conceal, suppress — used here to argue that concealment of knowledge/faith has always been a legitimate necessity

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir (AS) say in response to al-Hasan al-Basri's claim about those who conceal knowledge?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) refutes al-Hasan al-Basri's claim that those who conceal knowledge will torment the inhabitants of Hell with foul odors, deploying a reductio ad absurdum: if that were true, the celebrated Believer of Pharaoh's household (Quran 40:28), who concealed his faith to protect Prophet Moses (AS), would also be condemned. The Imam then declares that knowledge has always been concealed since the time of Noah (AS), and concludes definitively that true knowledge resides only with the Ahl al-Bayt — pointing to himself.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Washha, from Aban Bin Usman, from Abdullah Bin Suleyman who said,

‘I heard Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> saying, and in his<sup>asws</sup> presence was a man from the people of Al-Basra called Usman the blind one, and he was saying, ‘Al-Hassan Al-Basry is alleging that those who are concealing the knowledge would be harming the inhabitants of the Fire by a wind of their bellies’.

So Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So, destroyed then, is the Believer of the people of the Pharaoh<sup>la</sup>. The knowledge has not ceased to be concealed since Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Sent Noah<sup>as</sup>. Therefore, let Al-Hassan (Al-Basry) go right and left, for by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, he would not find the knowledge except over here’.
en.sarwar: 15. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla ibn Muhammad from al-Washsha’ from Aban ibn ‘Uthman from ‘Abdallah ibn Sulayman who has said the following.

‘(Imam) abu Ja‘far (a.s.) said to a man from Basra called ‘Uthman al-A’ma who would keep saying, “Al-Hassan al-Basri believes that those who hide knowledge the bad odor from their stomach will cause suffering to the people of hell.”

The Imam said, “The true believer of the people of Pharaoh is then destroyed. Knowledge from the time of Noah became veiled (s.a). Let Hassan go left and right. I swear by Allah he will not find knowledge in no other place but here with us.”
